# Worker01: complete source-defined stocks need bounded proposals or explicit blockers

The provisional 188-case shard contains nine decisions (seven source-qualified preparations) with recovered primary formulations, `proposal_ids: []`, and `missing_requirement: null`. They share a generic future-integration deferral. Preserving stocks separately from dry solutes is correct; it does not explain why a source-qualified proposal cannot be prepared.

This finding is bounded to the frozen decisions below, not all stock cases or a final-head approval. No source, mapping, role, or release change is approved by this issue.

| Case index | Source label | Verified source scope |
|---|---|---|
| 17 | CaCl2 solution (0.1 M)*** | [CS-P-NBRC-1339](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=1339): 0.1 M CaCl2 aqueous stock; distilled water and autoclaving are explicit. |
| 92 | CaCl2 solution | [CS-P-NBRC-1339](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=1339): The short label is locally resolved to that 0.1 M stock in M9-Phenanthrene, without global synonym promotion. |
| 101 | MgSO4 solution (1 M)*** | [CS-P-NBRC-1339](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=1339): 1 M MgSO4 aqueous stock; distilled water and autoclaving are explicit; no dry hydrate identity is inferred. |
| 66 | MgSO4 solution | [CS-P-NBRC-1339](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=1339): The short label is locally resolved to that 1 M stock in M9-Phenanthrene, without global synonym promotion. |
| 68 | Phenanthrene solution (250 mM) in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO)**** | [CS-P-NBRC-1339](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=1339): 250 mM phenanthrene in DMSO, filtered with DMSO-safe filters; solvent is explicitly supplied. |
| 116 | Tween 80 solution** | [CS-P-NBRC-881](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=881): Preparation lists Tween 80 50 g and distilled water 1 L; preserve added-water amount rather than assume measured final volume. |
| 107 | Bicarbonate solution (1.0 M)*** | [CS-P-NBRC-1321](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=1321): NaHCO3 8.4 g and distilled water 100 mL; CO2 saturation, sealed CO2 atmosphere and autoclaving are explicit. Existing 84 g/L overlap requires bounded ownership resolution. |
| 114 | Sulfide solution (1.0 M)******* | [CS-P-NBRC-1321](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=1321): Na2S·9H2O 24 g and distilled water 100 mL; filtration and N2 storage are explicit. |
| 128 | FeCl3 solution | [CS-P-JCM-1036](https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1036): FeCl3·6H2O 0.15 g and distilled water 300 mL, freshly prepared; source-qualified nested Solution B occurrences only. |

Required resolution: prepare source-qualified native proposals or document a concrete remaining scientific/ownership blocker for each case. Bind the long/short CaCl2 and MgSO4 labels only to their exact source occurrences. Resolve existing-owner/cross-worker overlap before integration. Preserve added-water amounts rather than assume final volume; do not guess hydration, merge stocks by their solute, or approve roles. Require native validation and independent review before publication.

Frozen decisions SHA-256: `5dbbf63b1736fbac74bc5f6457be48fb3613b3bd38a3ab4d4e37a279ce3ce704`. Frozen proposals SHA-256: `eb27d6de8b6a3403b131cb9ec1e21c65d300a2a977fa2acabdf6b463dcda1354`. Full case IDs, occurrence paths, source captures and original retrieval times are in `.temp/all-unmatched-20261107/preflight/w01-shard-coordinator-review-v1/finding-001-concentration-completeness.json`.

Primary capture SHA-256 bindings:

- `CS-P-NBRC-881`: `6bf300eade6e04eb3e0047615fbafeb7d8ce795758966df1d562c8462eba2565`.
- `CS-P-NBRC-1321`: `471a2ea8c7daff318ea0b79a4b7508d5be43f5b823d728d957bdeef3c3ad6e4b`.
- `CS-P-JCM-1036`: `b50c448cb435eda7dd35bb52c171e56db259c40f097332035990ec931d8ea22d`.

This is distinct from the previously corrected canary artifact findings in #1159. This reviewer has not performed live issue deduplication or posted an issue.

Coordinator deduplication: current open issues were inspected before filing. #1159 concerns the accepted canary artifacts; #811 and #868 concern other label-index/identity problems. None covers these nine provisional full-shard completeness decisions. This finding belongs to the source-review evidence being prepared for #1160; dependency #1158 remains unchanged.

At the campaign's frozen base `e000d66dd26ab053e9b17ce7bf8d3c873c3dde99`, `data/ingredients/mapped/Fatty_Acid_Mixture_See_Medium_No_266.yaml` uses CHEBI:35366 as its identity and carries fatty-acid molecular-class aliases/structure. The source is a prepared stock, not that class.

[JCM medium266](https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=266), “Fatty acid mixture”, specifies valeric, isovaleric, alpha-methylbutyric and isobutyric acids, 0.5g each, 20ml distilled water, and concentrated NaOH to pH7.5. [CHEBI:35366](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/chebi/terms?iri=http%3A%2F%2Fpurl.obolibrary.org%2Fobo%2FCHEBI_35366) is the fatty-acid molecular class. Its whole-stock exact identity is unsupported. No final solution volume or stereochemistry can be inferred from these recipe inputs.

The reviewed isolated proposal uses `kgmicrobe.ingredient:fatty_acid_mixture_see_medium_no_266`, removes inherited single-molecule properties, rejects the eight incompatible molecular-class aliases while preserving provenance, and transcribes six named inputs with UNMAPPED component references. Two generic historical mixture labels remain unapproved. No functional role is newly assigned. Existing WITHHOLD remains; this proposal is not publication approval.

Exact before-owner SHA256: `00aa192a2ce2f4acb1b752d3a478ca4e661c8e15e2f0039c9b22b608a10a7e6c`. JCM capture SHA256: `0054a5cdd60634511ec40a28bc6743000104c8152118dfc019e987afb8886321`. Evidence/proposed payload and separate skeptical review are under `reports/all_unmatched_20261107/worker-05/root/` and `reviews/` on branch `review/all-unmatched-w05-source-review-20261107`.

Follow-up: reconcile cross-shard owner dependencies, integrate through guarded writers, review complete changed-owner claims, synchronize maintained surfaces and SSSOM, and retain release holds until native admission is supported (#1165). Do not merge with the different JCM1130 five-acid VFA stock. Live all-state searches for the exact owner, fatty acid and 35366 found no dedicated issue; #718 remains the broader excluded-claim backlog. No maintained data or downstream build was changed by this review.
title: JCM266 fatty-acid stock is incorrectly identified as the CHEBI fatty-acid molecular class

The frozen Worker 1 shard proposes four new owners for two equivalent preparations. This concerns unpublished proposals; no maintained owners have been merged or changed.

| Preparation | Proposals | Primary evidence |
|---|---|---|
| CO2-saturated bicarbonate | `NSC-PROP-NBRC_1257_Bicarbonate_Solution` and `CS-PROP-NBRC1321_CO2_BICARBONATE_STOCK` | Both sources specify 8.4 g NaHCO3 plus 100 mL distilled water, CO2 saturation, sealed CO2 bottles and autoclaving. |
| Sulfide from nonahydrate | `NSC-PROP-NBRC_1257_Sulfide_Solution` and `CS-PROP-NBRC1321_SULFIDE_STOCK` | NBRC1257 uses 12 g Na2S·9H2O plus 50 mL water; NBRC1321 uses 24 g plus 100 mL. Both are nominally 1 M, filter sterilized and stored under N2. The batch scales differ by two; the evidence does not establish distinct preparations. |

Primary pages: [NBRC1257](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=1257) and [NBRC1321](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=1321). Exact captures and payloads are bound in the finding below.

Reconcile each pair to one proposed owner while preserving both source cases, every occurrence, raw labels, original batch scales and receiving-medium amounts. Source numbers alone do not define distinct substances. This does not establish equivalence with generic 84 g/L bicarbonate, neutralized sulfide or 5% sulfide. Preserve added-water amounts without asserting measured final volume; keep generic source-local labels non-resolving. The author/coordinator must select the retained proposal; this issue selects no identifier and authorizes no maintained-owner merge.

The same-source phenanthrene and Metal44 pairs were already reported by the worker and remain separate reconciliation items. Current open-issue deduplication found no tracker for these two cross-source pairs; #1163 concerns the earlier stock-completeness gap.

Evidence under `.temp/all-unmatched-20261107/preflight/w01-shard-coordinator-review-v2/`: `finding-003-duplicate-preparations.json`, SHA256 `8395d68231535cb509d7fef4b1d1ad3405498c50fc71d9e9ce259c5219749261`; peer `duplicate-addendum-v1/comparison.json`, SHA256 `1efe59deafe86709301536500ac9a885ab9b2d793144591c1b3ab8c92a573a26`. Frozen proposal manifest SHA256 `eb456ecef3f68b587a2f0281336f88b33679eb8d65a38f842661457ec05866f0`.

Require native validation and independent re-review of the reconciled final payloads. No role, component, mapping-release or whole-record approval follows from this issue.
title: Reconcile duplicate NBRC1257 and NBRC1321 stock proposals before integration

body:
Surfaced by the hardened matcher in #489, running against the real recipe tree. Not a defect in that PR — the link is correct — but a live ambiguity the old tooling structurally could not show.

## Two recipes, one name

```
CultureMech:002799  data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/gyps_medium.yaml
  original_name: GYPS MEDIUM
  Glucose, Yeast extract, Peptone, Sea Salt, MES

CultureMech:009837  data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/TOGO_M450_GYPS_Medium.yaml
  original_name: GYPS Medium
  Distilled water, Yeast extract, MES, Sea salts (Sigma), Glucose, Peptone, N2
```

Same core formulation from two sources; 009837 additionally lists water and an N2 atmosphere.

## Why this matters

MIM's `GYPS` record links to **CultureMech:002799**, and that choice is defensible — its evidence reads *"CultureMech additionally lists MES and Sea Salt and no starch"*, which describes 002799's five ingredients exactly. So the verification was done against that record and the link is right.

**But its uniqueness was never checked, and could not have been.** The old matcher indexed recipes in a one-value dict keyed on lower-cased name, so only one of the two `gyps_medium` recipes was ever visible; the curator saw whichever happened to be indexed last. That the surviving one was the correct one is luck, not process.

Now that the index is multi-valued, `GYPS` reports as ambiguous with both ids, which is the honest state.

## What to decide

Is `CultureMech:009837` a **duplicate** of 002799 (a CultureMech-side dedup, in #218/#219's neighbourhood) or a **distinct variant** worth its own record? If the latter, MIM's `GYPS` may warrant a second reference — the schema added in #489 supports `VARIANT_OF` for exactly this.

No change to the existing link is proposed here: `culturemech_reference.medium_id` already names 002799 unambiguously, which is the whole point of carrying an id rather than a name.

## Scale

This is one instance of a general condition: **2291 CultureMech names are shared by more than one recipe**, and `defined_freshwater_medium_cocl2` names 29. Any future link verified by name has the same exposure; the ambiguity flag in `reports/culturemech_link_candidates.tsv` is what makes it visible.
title: Two CultureMech recipes are both named gyps_medium — the GYPS link's uniqueness was never checkable

body:
## Problem

`data/ingredients/mapped/Distilled_Water.yaml` is grounded to generic
`CHEBI:15377 water`, but its live synonym list grades materially distinct water
preparations as `EXACT_SYNONYM`, including:

- `Tap water`
- `Double distilled water`
- `Demineralized water`
- `BOUND WATER`

This makes `docs/data/label_index.csv` resolve those recipe labels to the
Distilled water record as though the supplied materials were interchangeable.
They are not: tap-water composition is source-dependent, demineralization and
distillation are different processes, double-distilled water is a distinct
purity specification, and bound water is not a purchasable synonym for
distilled water.

The labels arrived through kg-microbe synonym enrichment, but ontology synonym
scope cannot override MIM's supplied-form identity rule. The same distinction
is now explicit in `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` section 3 and
`docs/HIERARCHY_GUIDE.md` after #448.

## Scope

- Review every synonym on the Distilled water record against recipe-level
  supplied-form identity.
- Remove or retype false `EXACT_SYNONYM` assertions without losing source
  provenance.
- Decide whether each recipe-relevant preparation needs its own record and
  ontology/registry/local grounding; do not collapse them merely because ChEBI
  supplies only generic water.
- Regenerate the label index and published exports after curation.
- Harden synonym enrichment so broad ontology synonym imports cannot silently
  turn distinct material grades/preparations into exact recipe-label identity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tap, double-distilled, demineralized, and bound water are not published as
      exact synonyms of Distilled water unless evidence establishes literal
      supplied-form identity.
- [ ] All retained raw labels preserve their source/provenance.
- [ ] Label-index resolution reflects the reviewed dispositions.
- [ ] A regression prevents the enrichment path from recreating these false
      exact synonyms.
- [ ] No water/purity hierarchy is invented in MIM; any future relationship
      model follows the stable-record contract tracked in #236/#447.

Related: #448, #232, #236, #447.
title: Review false exact synonyms that collapse distinct water preparations into Distilled water

body:
Found in adversarial review of #528 (pre-existing; that PR neither caused nor worsened it).

17 records carry the same synonym text twice, compared casefolded:

```
Distilled_Water.yaml            'sterile dh2o'
Alk_So42.yaml                   'aluminum potassium sulfate'
Na2glycerophosphate5h2o.yaml    'na2glycerophosphate•5h2o(cas: 13408-09-8)'
Casein_Peptone.yaml             'casein hydrolysate', 'casein enzymic hydrolysate'
```

Count is identical on `origin/main`, so this predates the surface-form work. The
backfill's own duplicate check kept it from growing.

Low severity, but not nothing:

* `export_lists.py` emits one `label_index.csv` row per synonym, so a duplicate
  synonym produces two identical index rows for the same record. The lookup still
  resolves, but the index is larger than the corpus it describes and row counts stop
  being a usable measure of coverage — which is the number this work has been tracking
  throughout.
* The builder pipes synonyms into SSSOM `other`, where `_pipe` caps at
  `MAX_OTHER_ENTRIES = 50`. On a crowded row a duplicate consumes a slot that a distinct
  surface form would otherwise get, and the cap is documented as biting hardest on the
  hydrate families.

The fix is a de-duplicating pass over `synonyms`, casefolded, keeping the first
occurrence and preferring the more specific `synonym_type` when the duplicates disagree
(e.g. a `RAW_TEXT` and an `EXACT_SYNONYM` of the same string). Worth pairing with a guard
so it cannot recur, since several writers append synonyms and only some check first.
title: 17 records carry the same synonym twice, inflating the label index and the other cap
